utility.notes: Confirmed via the Hawaii Public Utilities Commission's own page (which names Hawai'i Electric Light Company as the utility serving 'The Big Island', one of four PUC-regulated electric utilities, each island having its own unconnected grid) and Hawaiian Electric's own corporate site. HELCO is a subsidiary of Hawaiian Electric Industries operating under its own tariff for Hawaii Island, distinct from HECO (Oahu) and MECO (Maui).

value.name: Hawaii Electric Light Company (HELCO)
value.notes: Hawaiian Electric's Smart Renewable Energy (Smart DER) framework — SRE Export, SRE Non-Export, and Bring Your Own Device Plus — is a company-wide program described on Hawaiian Electric's own site without an island-specific carve-out, so this record reuses the same statewide-HEI-family program facts documented in hi-honolulu-honolulu-heco.json (see that record's generation_supplier.notes for the fuller Smart DER description), applied here at moderate confidence since this session did not independently reload a HELCO-specific page confirming identical terms apply to Hawaii Island.

city.notes: Hawaii County (the entire island of Hawai'i / 'the Big Island') is governed by a single county government with two Department of Public Works Building Division offices — East Hawai'i (Hilo) and West Hawai'i (Kailua-Kona) — rather than separate incorporated municipalities. This record represents the county-wide AHJ; per the mission's Hawaii-specific instruction, no separate sub-county city pages are created beneath it. 'Hilo' is used as the representative city/county-seat identifier.

permit_authority.value: County of Hawai'i Department of Public Works, Building Division

battery_programs.notes: Not independently confirmed for HELCO's Hawaii Island territory specifically this session; see generation_supplier notes.

value.name: Location/site plan showing major structures (1"=20' or larger preferred)
value.required_when: always, for both building and electrical submittals

value.name: Roof plan (1"=8') showing PV array with 3' clear space along the roof ridge, array supports, framing members, and mounting structure construction
Standard electrical diagram showing PV array configuration, wiring, overcurrent protection, inverter, disconnects, required markings/labels, and AC connection to the building
Specification sheets and installation manuals for all manufactured components (PV modules, inverters, combiner box, mounting system)
Two sets of drawings/site plans stamped by a Hawai'i-registered electrical engineer (per Hawai'i County Code Chapter 9, Sec. 9-33(b) and HRS Section 444)
value.required_when: always, for all residential and non-residential PV installations

value.name: Completed Building Permit Worksheet and Electrical Permit Application
Framing plan showing rafter-strengthening detail
value.required_when: only if combined PV array weight exceeds 5 lbs/sq ft, rafters are over-spanned per the guide's supplied span tables, or per-attachment dead load exceeds 45 lbs

value.name: Licensed Hawai'i state architect or structural engineer review/approval (professional stamp)
value.required_when: only for Iron Ridge/Unirac/Solar Mount roof-mounted systems installed above 30 ft, OR within Wind Exposure D (within 1/4 mile of the ocean), OR within Seismic Zones E or F — per County PV Bulletin PV 2012-01

required_documents.notes: Extracted directly from the County's own 'Guidelines for Permitting a Residential Photovoltaic (PV) System' (rev. 10.10.12) and its attached PV Bulletin PV 2012-01 (Aug. 24, 2012), read via PDF extraction of the County's own document.

value: Building and electrical inspections may be requested in any order following installation of panels on the roof (per PV Bulletin PV 2012-01)
For roof-mounted systems, the Building Division provides ladders to inspectors; in the interim, contractors must provide ladders and fall protection at the time of inspection

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited Permit Process for PV Systems
other_conditions: All photovoltaic systems for residential and non-residential installations require a building permit (Hawai'i County Code Chapter 9, Sec. 9-33(b))
Electrical design drawings and specifications must bear the approval of a Hawai'i-registered electrical engineer
Permits are issued only to Hawai'i State licensed building, electrical, or photovoltaic contractors (HRS Section 444)
Fasteners must not occur in roof framing beyond the exterior wall line without engineered calculations

Roof-mounted systems using Iron Ridge, Unirac, or Solar Mount mounting systems are pre-approved (no professional stamp required) up to 30 ft height in Wind Zones A/B/C and Seismic Zones A/B/C/D; systems in Wind Exposure D (within 1/4 mile of the ocean) or Seismic Zones E/F require licensed architect/structural engineer review
No material deviation from reviewed plans/specifications is permitted without prior electrical-engineer-of-record approval

value.name: Electrical permit fee — alternate energy power source (generators, capacitors, reactors, transformers), not more than 5 kW
value.notes: Hawai'i County Code Chapter 9, Section 9-40(q). 1 kW is treated as equivalent to 1 kVA for this fee.

value.name: Electrical permit fee — alternate energy power source, over 5 kW but not over 15 kW
Electrical permit fee — alternate energy power source, over 15 kW
Building permit fee — $0 to $500 estimated valuation
value.notes: Hawai'i County Code Chapter 5, Section 5-35, Table 1-A.

value.name: Building permit fee — $501 to $2,000 estimated valuation
value.unit: plus $1.50 per additional $100 or fraction thereof up to $2,000
value.notes: Hawai'i County Code Chapter 5, Section 5-35, Table 1-A.

value.name: Building permit fee — $2,001 to $25,000 estimated valuation
value.unit: plus $7.50 per additional $1,000 or fraction thereof up to $25,000
value.notes: Hawai'i County Code Chapter 5, Section 5-35, Table 1-A.

permit_fees.notes: Both the electrical permit fee (specific to alternate energy power sources, tiered by system kW) and the general building permit fee (tiered by estimated construction valuation) apply, since a PV installation requires both a building permit and an electrical permit under Hawai'i County Code. Higher building-permit valuation tiers ($25,001-$50,000 and $50,001+) also exist in the source table but are less relevant to typical residential PV systems and were omitted for brevity; see source PDF for the complete table.
